extracted.intended_audience: Wikipedia editors (especially those involved in creating, reviewing, or deleting news-related articles)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Wikipedia editors on how to apply notability, event, news, and BLP-related policies to topics derived from recent news; addresses common misinterpretations about 'no breaking news' rules and how to judge permanence and independence of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Myth: 'Breaking news shall not be covered by a new Wikipedia article'
rubrics_metrics.description: "Breaking news shall not be covered by a new Wikipedia article.  It does not matter if the news is published as a top story in newspapers on five continents.  It does not matter if it is verifiable or true.  It does not matter if it is covered neutrally.  Wikipedia is an encyclopedia and it must always be at least two or three years out of date.  Any story based on recent news reports should be deleted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This quoted 'policy' is a common misstatement — there is no such blanket policy. The essay calls this a myth and warns editors not to treat recency alone as a reason for deletion. Recent coverage can establish notability; do not delete solely because a topic is recent.

rubrics_metrics.name: WP:NOTNEWS — do not treat breaking news differently
rubrics_metrics.description: WP:NOTNEWS says "breaking news should not be emphasized or otherwise treated differently from other information."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although WP:NOTNEWS contains language excluding "routine news reporting on things like announcements, sports, or celebrities," that wording is intended to refer to the bulk of routine local newspaper content (wedding announcements, local sports) and should not be read to bar coverage of news that is picked up by other newspapers or cited in serious research. In short, breaking news should not receive sensational emphasis, but notable news that meets other guidelines may be covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: WP:NTEMP — notability is not temporary
rubrics_metrics.description: WP:NTEMP says "Notability is not temporary: once a topic has been the subject of 'significant coverage' in accordance with the general notability guideline, it does not need to have ongoing coverage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means that notability can be established immediately by sufficient independent coverage and, once established, is permanent; editors should not try to predict long-term significance or require future coverage as proof of notability.

rubrics_metrics.name: WP:Notability (books) — book notability requires independent, in-depth coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: WP:Notability (books) deems a book notable if it "has been the subject of multiple, non-trivial published works ... such as newspaper articles."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage must be independent of the book's publisher and must go beyond simple description of the plot. In-depth newspaper articles and reviews can satisfy this standard; superficial mentions do not.

rubrics_metrics.name: WP:EVENT — event/article notability is probabilistic and context-dependent
rubrics_metrics.description: WP:EVENT includes classes of local news which "may or may not be" notable and offers advice about news stories from a single source or from tabloids; it talks in terms of probability rather than drawing a firm line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because WP:EVENT is deliberately non-prescriptive, editors should avoid using prejudices to decide what is worthy of coverage; instead consider breadth of coverage, number and independence of sources, and whether the event affects a widespread social group versus only a minority. Single-source or tabloid-only coverage is more likely insufficient, but the guideline requires case-by-case judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: WP:BLP1E — extra caution for biographies of living persons
rubrics_metrics.description: WP:BLP1E concerns biographies of living persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should be cautious when creating or naming biography articles based on recent negative events; while some editors cope with the guideline by giving temporary, narrowly negative titles (e.g., 'Arrest of X'), this is an unfortunate workaround and should not be an automatic reason for deletion. BLP concerns require careful sourcing and neutral scope; articles usually find an appropriate name and scope over time.
